title: How Going First Turns a Man Into Someone Worth Following
caption:
A man of God moves first into the cost. Not the guy giving orders from a safe distance.

You know the guy you owe an apology. Waiting him out feels like strength, but it's really two guys stuck in the same fight. Going first means you send it tonight: "I was wrong, I'm sorry." That costs your pride before it gets you anything back.

In the group project, the late shift, the family blowup, somebody's going to eat the cost. A godly man doesn't wait to see who it'll be. He steps into it first, before a single finger starts pointing.

"While we were still sinners, Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8). He didn't wait for anyone to earn it. He moved into the worst of it first, before a single man deserved it. That's the leadership you're actually copying every time you go first.

Guys don't follow the loudest voice in the room. They follow the one who already took the hit before he asked anyone else to. Every time you go first, a brother watching learns your word costs you something. That's what trust is built on.

Who do you owe a text tonight?
